sara: Heads up — profiling shows a ~12% p99 regression for streaming responses after yesterday's runtime deploy. Traces point at higher flush cadence and much more partial-decode preemption. Anyone seen this?
vikram: Which trace id / which commit? did kernel routing change too?
sara: trace-id: 0xabc123 (from 2026-03-10T14:03:12Z). Quick perf counter dump from the canary node:
```
stream_flushes/sec: 34
avg_batch_size: 3.2
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.78
partial_decode_preempts: 0 -> 12  # big jump since deploy
cpu_decoder_loop_wcet_ms: +20
```
elliot: partial_decode_preempts jump is the red flag for me. That tends to thrash the decoder and hurts p99.
marta: I pushed commit 87c4 (adaptive-token-budget) yesterday — it changed per-request token_budget target to be dynamic based on queue weight. That may cause many small streaming requests to trigger early flushes.
vikram: Also yesterday's kernel-routing tweak prefers the "small-kernel" path for streaming routes; small-kernel shows worse per-token decoder loop perf when partial-decode is used (microbenchmarks showed this at seq 64-128).
sara: Repro on staging: forcing token_budget back to 8 for streaming routes reduces flushes/sec from 34 -> 18 and preempts drop to 3. So it's likely the token_budget change + kernel routing combo.
perf-bot: CI perf run: baseline vs 87c4: streaming-p99 +11%, streaming-q95 flat.
elliot: Short plan: (A) rollback adaptive token_budget for streaming-only routes, (B) add a 1-token grace in partial-decode scheduler to avoid immediate preemption churn, (C) add KV cache warmup for multi-request conversational sessions.
marta: For warmup — we need to prefetch KV keys at admission time only for requests with context_len > 64 to avoid extra work for tiny chats.
vikram: Also tweak kernel cost model: prefer hybrid/higher-throughput kernel for seq_len 64-128 when partial-decode is enabled. Small-kernel is optimized for memory but not for preempt-heavy flows.
sara: I'm going to push a canary: runtime flag streaming.token_budget_forced=8, partial_decode.grace_tokens=1, and admission.kv_prefetch_threshold=64. Rolling to canary group now.
ryan: Add metrics: streaming.preemptions_per_stream and kv.warmup_hit_rate so we can observe impact.
sara: Canary results after 30m: p99 delta reduced to +3% vs baseline, avg_batch_size up slightly, preempts down to 2-4 per window. kv_warmup_hit_rate ~0.92.
elliot: Good improvement. Next: run microbench of small-kernel vs hybrid for seq 64/96/128 with partial-decode enabled. If hybrid wins, update kernel routing cost model.
marta: Filed follow-up issue: infra#412 - "kernel-cost-tuning for streaming partial-decode". I'll own the bench.
vikram: Also add canary to test with higher concurrency to ensure no regressions at 90th percentile throughput.
perf-bot: Note: reverting adaptive token_budget for streaming will affect cost targets — coordinate with optimize team if we keep revert longer than 24h.
sara: Will coordinate. Thanks all. :pray:
summary: Investigated streaming p99 regression post-deploy. Root cause: interaction of adaptive token_budget + small-kernel routing causing higher flush cadence and partial-decode preempts. Canary forcing token_budget=8 + grace token + kv prefetch reduced p99. Follow-ups: kernel cost model bench, additional metrics, coord with Optimize for cost impact.
